# `Scanner/PhantomQA-v0` · Phantom QA: measure, judge and diagnose

**C · The system** · quality control · kind 1, measure · isolates C31: From a failed test to its cause. [The map](../../docs/tasks.md)

**Status:** ADMITTED: on 300 fresh instances per level the reference passes >= 98 %, no policy that ignores the object passes more than 3 % (95 % bounds)

The physicist's part of phantom QA. Each test of the guidance can be failed by more than one fault (a gradient miscalibration or a shim error; the transmit field or a receive element; signal instability or a loose phantom), so the QA scan says which test fails and a second scan, chosen for that test, says why.

Kind of task: **{'rule': 'open_loop within 25 points of the reference = measurement task, else decision task', 'levels': {'1': {'kind': 'measurement', 'reference': 1.0, 'open_loop': 1.0, 'gap_points': 0.0, 'n': 300}, '2': {'kind': 'measurement', 'reference': 1.0, 'open_loop': 1.0, 'gap_points': 0.0, 'n': 300}, '3': {'kind': 'measurement', 'reference': 0.9967, 'open_loop': 0.77, 'gap_points': 22.7, 'n': 300}}, 'source': 'mrgym gate Scanner/PhantomQA-v0 --n 300 --write on mrgym-engine-0.3.0, 2026-11-27'}**.

| Given | Deliver | Scored by |
|---|---|---|
| The uniform section of the ACR large phantom in a scanner with zero, one or two hidden faults; the site's ACR T1 protocol; the limits of the ACR guidance; a closed list of seven faults; a scan-time budget | The four test quantities measured on the ACR T1 scan, the tests that fail, and the faults of the system | A noise-free scan of the same protocol on the hidden system: the values must agree with the verifier's measurement, the verdicts with the guidance's limits, the faults with the hidden state |

## World

- On the table: ACR large phantom, slice 7 (world kind acr), 1.5 T or 3 T
- Sequences that matter here: se, afi, spgr
- Formulas the agent is given: edges at half the water signal; PIU; ghosting ratio; a distortion from a field gradient scales with 1 / bandwidth and follows the readout axis; a ratio of two images acquired with the same coil cancels the receive profile

| Hidden (measurable only by scanning) | Told |
|---|---|
| which faults are present and their sizes | the phantom and its diameter |
| gradient calibration, shim, transmit and receive profiles | the ACR T1 protocol of the site |
| position of the phantom (within 1 mm, 0.3 degrees) | the definitions of the four quantities |
| noise level | the limits and the tolerances |
| the 128-bit world seed | the closed fault list with the test each fault moves |
|  | the instrument datasheet |
|  | realised protocol, timing and cost of every plan and scan |

## Deliverable and reward

- Deliverable: `submit` with `{'measured': {'diameter_y_mm': '<number>', 'diameter_x_mm': '<number>', 'piu_percent': '<number>', 'ghosting_ratio': '<number>'}, 'failed_tests': ['<test>'], 'faults': ['<fault>']}`
- Reward range [0.0, 1.0]; paid only at submit; 0 on every other step
- Gates: the scanner log replays and is within budget; at least one accepted scan
- Error: `largest over the four quantities of |delivered - measured| / tolerance`
- Score: `none: the reward is 1 for a pass and 0 otherwise`
- Passing: all gates; every quantity within its tolerance; the failed tests and the faults exactly right

## Gate: the control policies on fresh instances

Run 2026-11-27 on engine `mrgym-engine-0.3.0`, package 0.1.0.dev0: `mrgym gate Scanner/PhantomQA-v0 --n 300 --write` (split gate, seeds 0..299; recipes tuned on split tune, seeds <set 0..2>:<0..15>). A level is admitted when the lower bound of the reference is at least 90 %, the upper bound of every must-fail policy is at most 10 % and every ablation required at the level loses at least 25 points (lower bound of the paired difference). Bounds are one-sided, 95 %. Cells: passed / instances (rate; bound).

| Policy | Must | Level 1 | Level 2 | Level 3 | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `prior` | fail | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | 0/300 (0.0 %; upper bound 1.0 %) | no scan; nominal values, every test passes, no fault |

## What the agent reads at reset (level 2, seed 0)

~~~text
# Phantom QA: measure, judge and diagnose
The scanner is a 3 T system. The uniform section (slice 7) of the ACR large
phantom lies at the isocentre: a disc of solution, 190 mm inner diameter. The scanner may have a fault, two, or none.

1. Run the site's ACR T1 scan and measure on its image:
    sequence se, tr_ms 500, te_ms 20, fov_mm 250, matrix 256, slice_mm 5, averages 1,
    bandwidth_hz_per_px 130, pe_dir y (phase encoding along y, readout along x).
  diameter_y_mm, diameter_x_mm   edge to edge through the centre of the phantom along y, edges at half the mean signal of the 200 cm^2 circle (radius 79.8 mm) centred on the isocentre; the same along x
  piu_percent                    100 (1 - (high - low) / (high + low)): highest and lowest mean of a 1 cm^2 circle (radius 5.64 mm) lying entirely inside the 200 cm^2 circle (radius 79.8 mm) centred on the phantom
  ghosting_ratio                 |((top + bottom) - (left + right)) / (2 large)|: large = mean of the 200 cm^2 circle; the others = mean of 16 x 63 mm rectangles in the background, centred 110 mm from the isocentre, the 63 mm side tangential (top, bottom: along x; left, right: along y)
  (profile gives the numbers along a line, and with samples = 1 the mean of a rectangle; read_regions the mean of circles.)
2. Judge the tests of the ACR guidance:
  geometric_accuracy     fails when a diameter is outside 190 +- 3 mm
  intensity_uniformity   fails when piu_percent is below 80
  ghosting               fails when ghosting_ratio is above 0.03
3. Name every fault of the system. The closed list (a fault moves the test named in brackets):
  gradient_x         [geometric_accuracy] the X gradient (left-right, image columns) is miscalibrated: lengths along x are wrong by the same percentage in every protocol
  gradient_y         [geometric_accuracy] the Y gradient (anterior-posterior, image rows) is miscalibrated: lengths along y are wrong by the same percentage in every protocol
  shim               [geometric_accuracy] the shim left a linear B0 gradient across the phantom: the image is stretched or compressed along the readout axis, in proportion to 1 / bandwidth
  b1_transmit        [intensity_uniformity] the transmit field is too high or too low near the centre of the phantom (the flip angle is off there)
  receive_coil       [intensity_uniformity] a receive coil element is down: the receive sensitivity falls off across the phantom
  signal_instability [ghosting] the signal amplitude varies from pulse to pulse (transmitter, receiver or gradient amplifier)
  phantom_motion     [ghosting] the phantom is not fixed: it rocks along the phase-encode axis during the scan
  A failed test is not a diagnosis: more than one fault moves each test. A failed test has exactly one fault. The
  scan-time budget leaves room after the QA scan for a short scan of your own design that tells them apart. A fault
  in the list is either present (its test fails) or absent; small imperfections that fail no test are not faults.

Deliver with `submit`: the four measured values, the failed tests, the faults. Passing: each value within
0.6 mm, 3 PIU points, and 0.006 or 15 % of the ratio (whichever is larger) of the scanner's own
noise-free measurement on the scan above; the failed tests exactly those that fail; the faults exactly those present.
The scanner's log must show that you measured. An answer in the wrong unit is wrong.

Limits. Scan time: 156.5 s (only `scan` spends it). Tool calls: 64 (every call counts once unless rejected). Rejected calls: 8 (a call refused for how it is written: unknown name, wrong type; costs nothing else), of them at most 3 refused `submit` calls. The episode ends at `submit` or at a limit; without `submit` the score is 0.
[scan time left 156.50 of 156.5 s · calls 0/64 · rejected 0/8]
~~~

## Determinism and versions

same (seed, level, tool calls) -> same observations, log hash chain and reward; a repeated scan draws new noise; the verifier's scan is noise-free.

Rewards are comparable only within one environment version (the `-vN` suffix) and one scanner engine (`mrgym --version`).
